# omx-clap-core / fuzz_preset

omx-clap-core's own fuzz target `fuzz_preset` ([source](source/fuzz_preset.c), modified; see below), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-clap-core 0.20.1 (FreeMixer/omx-clap-core at 246923f0).

Hands the input, as a whole preset file of at most 3 MiB, to the JSON reader pj_parse, and checks the result against the harness's own reading of the JSON grammar the header states (nesting at most 32 deep). An accepted file is written back compact and pretty with pj_write, compared byte for byte with the harness's own rendering, read again to the same tree, and rewritten with its modifiedAt member set as a save does. The file is then read again, and written again, with one allocation failing, chosen by the input's bytes.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Changed by OSS Verify in two files, fuzz/fuzz_preset.c and fuzz/alloc.c (both in source/ as built): once malloc or realloc returns NULL, to the harness or to the reader, the call ends and returns 0, after a reading that ran out is checked to be refused cleanly. A NULL on a request of more than PJ_ALLOC_BOUND of the input is not memory running out: the checks judge it. No library code changes.
- Why: in the ASan builds each size class of the allocator has a fixed region of 3.5 GiB, and freed memory is held in quarantine, so on a large input (3 MB of nested arrays) a reading can run out of memory where the plain build does not. The reader then refuses the file correctly, and the harness aborted on that correct refusal.
- Linked against a static libomx-clap-readers.a of src/preset_file.c and src/lv2_locate.c of omx-clap-core 0.20.1 at commit 246923f0, and the changed fuzz/alloc.c (source/alloc.c), compiled with each build's flags, as omx-clap-core's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- As in omx-clap-core's own fuzz build, the readers are compiled with fuzz/alloc.h forced on them, so their malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup and free go to fuzz/alloc.c, which counts the bytes the reader holds and can make one chosen allocation fail; the harness's own allocations use the C library directly.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The file read from three copies followed by different bytes ('1', '2', NUL) gets the same answer each time, and the same tree whenever two of them are accepted: the reader reads nothing past the end of the file. The three are compared only when memory did not run out; a reading that ran out must be refused cleanly instead ([lines 499-559](source/fuzz_preset.c#L499-L559)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- While reading a file of n bytes the reader holds at most 256 n bytes plus a constant for the 32 open containers and 4096 more ([lines 561-567](source/fuzz_preset.c#L561-L567)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The reader accepts exactly the files the harness's own grammar reads (JSON with nesting at most 32 deep, no \u0000, surrogates only in pairs, the stated number form), and reads each to the tree the harness reads from it: types, member names in order, string bytes, number text and value ([lines 570-590](source/fuzz_preset.c#L570-L590)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A refused file leaves the tree all zero bytes and gives back every byte the reader allocated while refusing it ([lines 592-609](source/fuzz_preset.c#L592-L609)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The file read again with one of its allocations failing is refused cleanly in the same way; a write, pretty or compact, with one of the writer's allocations failing returns no text and holds no memory ([lines 614-665](source/fuzz_preset.c#L614-L665)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An accepted tree written compact and pretty is, byte for byte, the harness's rendering of the writer's format, and reads back to the same tree ([lines 669-711](source/fuzz_preset.c#L669-L711)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Setting modifiedAt on an accepted object, then writing and reading it back, keeps every other member with its name, value and place, sets an existing modifiedAt in place or appends a new one, and holds the value set ([lines 715-769](source/fuzz_preset.c#L715-L769)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
